title: Scalable Second-order Riemannian Optimization for $K$-means Clustering
claim: Local search from random starts reliably reaches second-order critical points, and these are globally optimal with zero error.
layout: 3 panels in a row, shared iterations axis, many overlaid run curves
description: A single row of three line plots that share an x-axis of iterations (0 to about 800). Each panel overlays dozens of thin trajectories from independent runs on a pale grey background with white grid lines. The left panel, in blue, shows global suboptimality on a log scale. It falls from about 10^3 to below 10^-10 around iterations 450 to 800. The middle panel, in red, shows gradient norm on a log scale. It is noisy and large at first, then drops sharply to about 10^-6 to 10^-7. The right panel, in green, shows the minimum Hessian eigenvalue. It starts strongly negative and noisy, then rises and plateaus at positive values. Together they show convergence to a global optimum that is also a second-order critical point. The eye goes first to the steep blue drop on the left.
caption: Local convergence to second-order critical points yields global optimality. In the GMM setting, where ground-truth partitions can be planted, we consistently observe local convergence to the global optimum, yielding zero clustering error. This provides strong numerical evidence that near-second-order critical points are near-globally optimal, as hypothesized in Assumption [ref].
abstract: Clustering is a hard discrete optimization problem. Nonconvex approaches such as low-rank semidefinite programming (SDP) have recently demonstrated promising statistical and local algorithmic guarantees for cluster recovery. Due to the combinatorial structure of the $K$-means clustering problem, current relaxation algorithms struggle to balance their constraint feasibility and objective optimality, presenting tremendous challenges in computing the second-order critical points with rigorous guarantees. In this paper, we provide a new formulation of the $K$-means problem as a smooth unconstrained optimization over a submanifold and characterize its Riemannian structures to allow it to be solved using a second-order cubic-regularized Riemannian Newton algorithm. By factorizing the $K$-means manifold into a product manifold, we show how each Newton subproblem can be solved in linear time. Our numerical experiments show that the proposed method converges significantly faster than the state-of-the-art first-order nonnegative low-rank factorization method, while achieving similarly optimal statistical accuracy.
